_readme: Principal spatial templates extracted from real museum floor plans (multi-agent extraction 2026-07-21, 8 museums, 8/8 agents clean). Each template abstracts the museum's principal idea into the /template-maps cell vocabulary; tiles are merged into template_patterns.json (mode stamp) for the editor and map making. Provenance: literature+abstraction — templates PROPOSE (P-10); numbers carry their sources. Validation: dims/tokens/top-to-bottom walkability/stop pockets, results per entry.

museums.architect: Giorgio Vasari, 1560-1581 (completed by Buontalenti and Parigi; Tribuna by Buontalenti, 1584)
museums.circulation_type: enfilade off a U-shaped spine corridor (single-loaded statue-lined corridor with lateral room enfilade)
museums.mechanism: The U-corridor separates flow from seeing: movement, daylight, and the long end-stopped vista belong to the statue-lined spine, while stationary looking is decanted into optional enfilade rooms one door off the spine, so stopping to see never blocks the walk.

museums.walk_rule: Enter at the head of the east spine and walk the 3-wide corridor pulled forward by the hero visible on-axis 27 cells ahead, dipping optionally through door gaps into three side rooms whose aligned doors form a second parallel vista, then turn west along the south corridor past the hero and exit on the enfilade axis.
museums.pacing_rule: Paired podium statues line the spine's inner wall in bays broken by door gaps (Vasari's three-bays-plus-narrow-bay rhythm), and every pause option sits off the clear lane so lingering never dams the flow; the one mandated stop is the raised dais step before the end-stopped hero.

museums.museum: Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
museums.circulation_type: forced single path (continuous spiral ramp; abstracted as switchback serpentine)
museums.mechanism: By collapsing all circulation into one gently sloped descending ramp, the plan removes route choice entirely — flow is automatic — while shallow web-wall bays create stop pockets just off the moving path and the open central void lets visitors preview and re-encounter works across the atrium before and after passing them.

museums.walk_rule: Enter at the top (the elevator drop-off) and walk one un-branching serpentine: each 3-wide lane runs the full width, turns through a 3-cell gap at the alternating end of each partition, and empties onto the rotunda floor at the bottom where the hero stands on the atrium axis.
museums.pacing_rule: Movement never pauses the route — art bays are recessed into the solid partition stretches as stop pockets beside the flow, while the aligned see-through void windows (c6-c8) form the atrium axis that promises the hero podium from up to 27 cells away and re-shows passed works across lanes.

museums.mechanism: By clearing the entire 50 m span of structure and putting art on freestanding walls and suspended panels, the plan makes flow and seeing the same act — the visitor self-routes through a matrix of view-objects, and no wall ever hides the next work for long.

museums.walk_rule: Enter anywhere on the open top edge and drift freely through a column-free field; freestanding picture-walls and podia are obstacles to orbit, not corridors to follow, and the only fixed event is the on-axis hero at the hall's centre.
museums.pacing_rule: Pacing comes from paired off-axis freestanding walls at each third of the walk that slow the drift into eddies, while the untouched central axis keeps a 13-cell promise to the hero so the visitor always chooses between lingering and advancing.

museums.museum: Sir John Soane's Museum, 13 Lincoln's Inn Fields, London
museums.architect: Sir John Soane, 1792-1824 (house rebuilt in three campaigns; museum arranged until his death 1837)
museums.circulation_type: cabinet — a dense wunderkammer loop of tiny interconnected rooms threaded on narrow passages, with one end-stopped axial vista to the deepest point
museums.mechanism: Soane resolves flow versus seeing by making every wall of the narrow path itself the display and letting the eye outrun the body — layered apertures (colonnade screens, floor cuts to the crypt, folding picture-planes) show objects several rooms ahead, so walking is compressed to a shuffle while seeing is multiplied in depth.

museums.walk_rule: A 3-wide spine runs the full axis while staggered door gaps pull the body sideways into small 3x4 cabinet pockets; the eye keeps the long axial vista to the hero as the feet loop room by room.
museums.pacing_rule: Every five rows a cross-wall with corridor-facing niche slots compresses the walk back onto the spine, alternating pocket-dwell and corridor-glide, until the terminal dome room releases the width and the hero end-stops the 16-cell sightline just before a blind wall.

museums.circulation_type: forced single path: end-stopped enfilade with off-axis display (loop at building scale)
museums.mechanism: Aligned door openings fuse five rooms into one long axial vista that promises the terminus (flow), while every sculpture is displaced off that axis with its own facing direction — a network of gazes that pulls the walker sideways into stops — and the axis itself is end-stopped at the Cangrande hinge, where a single hero on a raised plinth owns a whole bay and is circled rather than passed.

museums.walk_rule: Enter on the central axis and cross four rooms through aligned 3-wide door gaps; in each room the works sit off-axis so you drift sideways to a stop pocket and return to the line, until the axis delivers you into the hero bay where you circle the raised podium and exit through the off-axis side door behind it.
museums.pacing_rule: The hero is visible from the entrance through every aligned gap (a 24-cell promise), but four cross walls each impose a pause-and-drift beat before the axis is allowed to resolve, and the end-stop wall plus sideways exit ensure the vista terminates on the hero instead of continuing past it.

museums.architect: Louis Métezeau & Jacques II Androuet du Cerceau, 1595–1607 (bay rhythm: Percier & Fontaine, 1805–1810; skylights: Lefuel, 1860s)
museums.circulation_type: forced single path — continuous axial promenade with walk-past wall hang, rhythmed by bays
museums.mechanism: A single very long, 13 m-wide axis keeps everyone flowing toward an endless vanishing point, while nine column-framed bays with overhead skylights pinch the walk into regular stopping pockets where the continuous wall hang can be faced one painting at a time.

museums.walk_rule: Enter on axis and drift down the wide central lane toward the hero visible from the first step; at each bay, step sideways into the wall pocket to face a slot, then rejoin the flow, finally rounding the end-stopped hero to exit.
museums.pacing_rule: Paired column cells pinch the 13-cell width every 4 rows into nine bays, and each bay's midpoint row carries a facing pair of wall slots — a metronome of stop-beats under one uninterrupted 33-cell sightline.

museums.museum: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa
museums.circulation_type: free-plan matrix — independent room-boxes floating in a multi-entry, non-hierarchical circulation field
museums.mechanism: Flow and seeing never compete because they occupy different spaces: movement is free in the daylight corridor-streets between boxes, while each artwork gets a sealed room individually tuned (size 18–324 m², height 4–12 m, light) to seeing it, entered and exited at the visitor's choice.

museums.walk_rule: Enter anywhere along the open top edge; parallel streets (west 3-wide, central 3-wide, east lane) and full-width cross streets loop around sealed room-boxes, and the central street's promised hero room dead-ends, sending the walker back into the field to choose an exit route.
museums.pacing_rule: Seeing is quantized into rooms — pace is the number of boxes you elect to enter and leave through the street field, not distance walked; corridor-hung slots give the streets themselves exhibition weight between stops.

museums.architect: Robert Venturi & Denise Scott Brown (VSBA, with Sheppard Robson), 1991
museums.circulation_type: enfilade — three parallel lines of galleries off a skewed axis; the central line is a true on-axis enfilade with false-perspective diminishing arches, the side lines have offset doorways that deliberately interrupt the vistas
museums.mechanism: The central nave-like enfilade makes one long promise — Cima's altarpiece glimpsed through five diminishing arches at the deepest point pulls flow forward — while the flanking rooms, entered through offset doors that break the lateral sightlines, decompress into small domestic-scale chambers where stopping and seeing individual panels is the default.

museums.walk_rule: Enter on-axis at the top and the hero is already visible 28 cells away through every door gap; the 3-wide central nave carries the flow straight to the raised hero chamber, while offset side doors peel viewers into 3-cell-wide cabinet rooms and return them to the axis one bay deeper.
museums.pacing_rule: Cross walls every 5-6 rows frame the vista and the door gaps narrow as you go (5, 5, 3, 3 cells) — a false perspective that makes the hero feel farther then suddenly near — with the final threshold stepping up onto a platform where the 3s altarpiece slot is end-stopped by the terminal wall and the exit turns off-axis, exactly as the wing hands you sideways to the bridge.
